abstract.p: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used for scientific writing and research assistance, yet their ability to maintain consistent citations across multi-turn conversations remains largely unexplored. This study introduces the concept of citation drift-the phenomenon where references mutate, disappear, or get fabricated during extended LLM interactions. Through a comprehensive analysis of 240 conversations across 4 LLaMA models using 36 authentic scientific papers from 6 domains, this work demonstrates significant citation instability. Results reveal that citation stability varies dramatically across models, with llama-4-maverick-17b showing the highest stability (0.481) and llama-4-scout-17b showing the worst fabrication rates (0.856). This study introduces novel metrics including citation drift entropy and willingness-to-cite, providing a framework for evaluating LLM citation reliability in scientific contexts. Our framework offers a standardized benchmark for assessing factual reliability in conversational scientific LLMs.
